cards.title: Sunday comes first
cards.prompt: What day of the week is the 25th?
cards.explain: This calendar starts its weeks on Sunday, and the 1st is a Monday. The 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th share a column, so the 25th is a Thursday.

cards.title: Leap day
cards.prompt: What day of the week is March 1st?

cards.explain: The bishop on a2 checks the king on g8 along the long diagonal. The knight on f5 is close but does not reach g8.

jev.context: A chess position with Black to move, drawn as a board with file letters and rank numbers.

cards.title: Mate or not
cards.prompt: White just played Qh7+. Is it checkmate?
cards.explain: The king can take the queen on h7: the bishop on b1 would guard it, but White's own pawn on e4 blocks the diagonal.

jev.context: A chess position with Black to move, drawn as a board with file letters and rank numbers. White just moved the queen to h7.
jev.instructions: Is Black checkmated in `card`?

cards.title: Three in a row
cards.prompt: X to move. Tap where X wins.
cards.explain: An X in the top right completes the top row. The middle right only blocks O.

jev.context: A tic-tac-toe board with red X marks and blue O marks; X is about to move.
jev.instructions: X has exactly one square that wins at once. Where is that square in `card`?

cards.title: Block it
cards.prompt: O to move. Tap where O must block.
cards.explain: X threatens the diagonal from the top left, so O must take the bottom right. The other diagonal is already blocked by the O in the bottom left.

jev.context: A tic-tac-toe board with red X marks and blue O marks; O is about to move.
jev.instructions: X threatens to win on exactly one square. Where must O play to block it in `card`?

cards.title: Four in a row
cards.prompt: Red to move. Tap the column that wins.
cards.explain: A red disc in column 4 lands on the fourth row and completes a diagonal from the bottom left. The red three on the second row cannot be finished yet: column 7 is empty.

jev.context: A connect four board with red and yellow discs; discs dropped into a column fall to the lowest empty hole. The columns are numbered 1 to 7 under the board.
jev.instructions: Red has exactly one column that wins at once. Where is that column in `card`?

cards.title: Sudoku
cards.prompt: Which number goes in the yellow cell?
cards.explain: The center row has 4, 8, 3 and 1, the center column has 7, 9, 6, 2, 1 and 8, and the center box adds nothing new. The only digit missing from all of them is 5.

jev.context: A 9 by 9 sudoku grid, partly filled in, with one empty cell highlighted in yellow and marked with a question mark.
jev.instructions: By the sudoku rules (each digit 1 to 9 once per row, column and 3 by 3 box), which digit must go in the highlighted cell in `card`?

cards.title: Best hand
cards.explain: The bottom row is a flush, five hearts, and a flush beats the straight from 5 to 9 on top.

jev.context: 2 rows of five playing cards on a green table; each row is one poker hand.
jev.instructions: By standard poker hand rankings, which row of cards is the winning hand in `card`?

cards.title: Best hand
cards.explain: Three sevens in the middle row beat the two pair (queens and jacks) on top and the ace-high bottom row.

jev.context: 3 rows of five playing cards on a green table; each row is one poker hand.
jev.instructions: By standard poker hand rankings, which row of cards is the winning hand in `card`?

cards.title: Fold the cube
cards.prompt: Fold this into a cube. Which number is opposite the 6?
cards.explain: Fold it with the 4 as the floor: 2 and 1 become the back and front walls, 6 and 3 the left and right walls, and 5 the lid. It is not a die, so the dice rule (opposite faces add up to 7) does not apply.

jev.context: A flat net of six squares, each with a number, that folds into a cube.
jev.instructions: If the net in `card` is folded into a cube, which number ends up on the face opposite the 6?

cards.title: Sink it
cards.prompt: One ship of four is left. Tap the square that sinks it.
cards.explain: The three hits run along row D from 3 to 5. A ship of four needs one more square in that row, and D6 is a miss, so it has to be D2.

jev.context: A battleship grid with rows A to H and columns 1 to 8, showing hits, misses and sunk ships, with a legend on the right. One ship, four squares long, is still afloat.
jev.instructions: Exactly one square must hold the last unhit part of the remaining ship. Where is that square in `card`?

jev.context: The outline of one country on its own, filled dark, north up, with no map, borders or labels around it.

cards.title: Name the shape
cards.explain: Chile runs about 4,300 km north to south but is rarely more than 350 km wide, breaking into islands at its southern tip.

jev.context: The outline of one country on its own, filled dark, north up, with no map, borders or labels around it.
jev.instructions: Which country has the outline shown in `card`?

cards.title: Name the shape
cards.explain: Four main islands in a curving arc, Hokkaido at the top, then Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu, make Japan.

jev.context: The outline of one country on its own, filled dark, north up, with no map, borders or labels around it.

cards.title: Name the shape

cards.title: Name the shape

jev.instructions: Which country has the outline shown in `card`?

cards.title: Mercator trap
cards.prompt: Which is bigger in real life?
cards.explain: DR Congo is about 2.33 million km2 and Greenland about 2.15 million; Mercator stretches land more the further it is from the equator, so Greenland looks several times bigger than it is.

jev.context: A Mercator map of the Atlantic and Africa with no labels; two countries are filled in colour and marked with letters.
jev.instructions: Which of the lettered countries in `card` has the larger real area on the ground?

cards.title: Mercator trap
cards.prompt: Which is bigger in real life?
cards.explain: Spain is about 506,000 km2 and Finland about 338,000, yet Mercator stretches Finland, far to the north, to look about twice the size of Spain.

jev.context: A Mercator map of Europe with no labels; two countries are filled in colour and marked with letters.
jev.instructions: Which of the lettered countries in `card` has the larger real area on the ground?

cards.title: Same scale
cards.explain: Brazil is about 8.5 million km2 and mainland Australia with Tasmania about 7.7 million, so Brazil is roughly a tenth bigger.

jev.context: Two countries drawn side by side at the same scale with an equal-area projection, each named underneath.
jev.instructions: Which of the two countries in `card` has the larger area?

cards.title: Next door
cards.prompt: Which country does NOT border Germany?
cards.explain: Slovakia lies east of Czechia and north of Hungary; Czechia and Austria sit between it and Germany.

jev.context: A map of central Europe with country borders and no labels, with Germany filled in orange.
jev.instructions: Which of these countries does not share a land border with Germany in `card`?

cards.title: Next door
cards.prompt: Which country does NOT border Brazil?
cards.explain: Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador; Peru and Colombia keep Ecuador away from it.

jev.context: A map of South America with country borders and no labels, with Brazil filled in orange.
jev.instructions: Which of these countries does not share a land border with Brazil in `card`?

cards.title: Next door
cards.prompt: Which country shares a land border with France?
cards.explain: French Guiana in South America is part of France, and its 730 km border with Brazil is the longest land border France has; Portugal, Austria and Denmark never touch France.

jev.context: A map of Europe, Africa and the Americas with country borders and no labels, with every part of France filled in orange.
jev.instructions: Which of these countries shares a land border with France, as shown in `card`?

cards.title: No neighbours
cards.prompt: Tap the country with no land border.
cards.explain: The Philippines is all islands with no land border; Indonesia is islands too, but shares Borneo with Malaysia, New Guinea with Papua New Guinea, and Timor with Timor-Leste.

jev.context: A map of Southeast Asia with country borders and no labels; four countries are filled in different colours and marked with letters.
jev.instructions: Which lettered country in `card` shares no land border with any other country?

cards.title: No coast
cards.explain: Hungary has no coast; Belgium has about 66 km on the North Sea, Slovenia about 47 km and Bosnia and Herzegovina about 20 km at Neum, both on the Adriatic.

jev.context: A map of central Europe and the Balkans with country borders and no labels; four countries are filled in different colours and marked with letters.
jev.instructions: Which lettered country in `card` has no coastline at all?

cards.title: No coast
cards.explain: Ethiopia lost its coast when Eritrea became independent in 1993; Sudan and Eritrea face the Red Sea and Kenya the Indian Ocean.

jev.context: A map of northeast Africa with country borders and no labels; four countries are filled in different colours and marked with letters.
jev.instructions: Which lettered country in `card` has no coastline at all?

cards.title: Find Egypt
cards.explain: Egypt sits in the northeast corner of Africa, where the Nile meets the Mediterranean; its Sinai peninsula reaches into Asia.

jev.context: A map of Africa with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Egypt in `card`?

cards.title: Find Paraguay
cards.explain: Paraguay is landlocked between Bolivia, Brazil and Argentina, yet it has one of the largest navies of any landlocked country.

jev.context: A map of South America with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Paraguay in `card`?

cards.title: Find Switzerland
cards.explain: Switzerland is wedged between France, Germany, Austria and Italy, in the middle of the Alps.

jev.context: A map of Europe with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Switzerland in `card`?

cards.title: Find Laos
cards.explain: Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia, squeezed between Thailand and Vietnam along the Mekong.

jev.context: A map of Asia with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Laos in `card`?

cards.title: Which country?
cards.explain: Mongolia sits between Russia and China and is the most sparsely populated sovereign country on Earth.

jev.context: A map of Asia with country borders and no labels, with one country filled in orange.
jev.instructions: Which country is filled in orange in `card`?

cards.title: Find Niger
cards.explain: Niger is the big landlocked country north of Nigeria; both are named after the Niger River, but Nigeria is the coastal one on the Gulf of Guinea.

jev.context: A map of West and North Africa with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Niger in `card`?

cards.title: Find Slovenia
cards.explain: Slovenia is the small country between Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia, with a short Adriatic coast; Slovakia lies further northeast, next to Poland.

jev.context: A map of Central Europe with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Slovenia in `card`?

cards.title: Find Iraq
cards.explain: Iraq lies between Syria and Iran around the Tigris and Euphrates, with only a tiny coastline at the top of the Gulf; Iran is the much larger country to its east.

jev.context: A map of the Middle East with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Iraq in `card`?

cards.title: Find Colombia
cards.explain: Colombia is in the northwest corner of South America, the only country on the continent with coasts on both the Pacific and the Caribbean.

jev.context: A map of South America with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Colombia in `card`?

cards.title: Find Madagascar
cards.explain: Madagascar is the large island off the southeast coast of Africa, across the Mozambique Channel.

jev.context: A map of Africa with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Madagascar in `card`?

cards.title: Find Finland
cards.explain: Finland lies between Sweden and Russia, east of the Gulf of Bothnia and north of the Gulf of Finland.

jev.context: A map of northern Europe with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Finland in `card`?

cards.title: Find Vietnam
cards.explain: Vietnam is the long S-shaped country along the eastern coast of the Indochinese peninsula, east of Laos and Cambodia.

jev.context: A map of Southeast Asia with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Vietnam in `card`?

cards.title: Find Kenya
cards.explain: Kenya sits on the equator on the Indian Ocean coast, between Tanzania to the south and Ethiopia and Somalia to the north.

jev.context: A map of East Africa with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Kenya in `card`?

cards.title: Find Portugal
cards.explain: Portugal is the narrow country on the Atlantic side of the Iberian Peninsula, west of Spain.

jev.context: A map of western Europe with country borders and no labels.
jev.instructions: Where is Portugal in `card`?

cards.title: Which country?
cards.explain: Bolivia is the landlocked country west of Brazil, between Peru and Chile on one side and Paraguay on the other.

jev.context: A map of South America with country borders and no labels, with one country filled in orange.
jev.instructions: Which country is filled in orange in `card`?

cards.title: Which country?
cards.explain: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America, between Honduras to the north and Costa Rica to the south, with coasts on both oceans.

jev.context: A map of Central America with country borders and no labels, with one country filled in orange.
jev.instructions: Which country is filled in orange in `card`?

cards.title: Which country?
cards.explain: Papua New Guinea is the eastern half of the island of New Guinea, north of Australia; the western half belongs to Indonesia.

jev.context: A map of Southeast Asia and Oceania with country borders and no labels, with one country filled in orange.

jev.instructions: Which country is filled in orange in `card`?

cards.title: Razorbill
cards.explain: The razorbill has a thick, blunt black bill crossed by a thin white line. The puffin's bill is big and striped orange, and the African penguin has a slim pointed bill and a black band across its chest.

jev.context: Three black and white seabirds standing upright on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which bird in `card` is the razorbill?

cards.title: Barn owl
cards.explain: The barn owl has a white heart-shaped face and dark eyes. The snowy owl is white all over with yellow eyes, and the eagle-owl has orange eyes and ear tufts.

jev.context: Three owls perched on stumps on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which owl in `card` is the barn owl?

cards.title: Toad
cards.explain: The toad has dry, warty skin, a squat body and short legs for crawling. The common frog has smooth, moist skin and long legs for leaping, and the red-eyed tree frog is a smooth green climber.

jev.context: Three amphibians sitting on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the toad?

cards.title: Which one is a dolphin
cards.explain: The orca, or killer whale, is the largest member of the dolphin family. The beluga is a toothed whale from a different family, the great white shark is a fish, and the manatee is a sea cow.

jev.context: Four large sea animals swimming on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is a dolphin?

cards.title: Ginkgo leaf
cards.explain: The ginkgo leaf is a little fan with fine veins running straight out from the stalk and a notch in its top edge. The oak leaf has rounded lobes, the maple leaf has five pointed lobes, and the horse chestnut leaf is a hand of separate leaflets.

jev.context: Four tree leaves lying flat on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which leaf in `card` is the ginkgo leaf?

cards.title: Iris
cards.explain: The iris has three petals standing up and three drooping "falls" with fuzzy yellow beards. The tulip is a smooth cup, the lily a flared trumpet with long stamens, and the daffodil has a trumpet in the middle of its petals.

jev.context: Four single flowers on their stems on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which flower in `card` is the iris?

cards.title: Chanterelle
cards.explain: The chanterelle is golden yellow and funnel-shaped, with blunt ridges that run down the stem instead of true gills. The fly agaric is red with white spots, the porcini has a brown bun cap on a fat stem, and the morel has a pitted honeycomb cap.

jev.context: Four wild mushrooms on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which mushroom in `card` is the chanterelle?

cards.title: Cowrie
cards.explain: The cowrie is a smooth, glossy, egg-shaped shell with no visible spiral. The scallop is a ribbed fan, the conch has spikes and a flared pink lip, and the nautilus is a striped coil.

jev.context: Four seashells on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which shell in `card` is the cowrie?

cards.title: Iguana
cards.explain: The green iguana has a big hanging dewlap under its chin, a row of spines down its back and a very long tail. The chameleon has turret eyes and a curled tail, and the bearded dragon is a flat, sandy lizard with a spiky beard.

jev.context: Three lizards on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which lizard in `card` is the iguana?

cards.title: Rhinoceros beetle
cards.explain: The rhinoceros beetle has a long curved horn growing up from its head, like a rhino. The stag beetle's "antlers" are a pair of giant jaws, and the ladybird has no horn at all.

jev.context: Three beetles seen from above on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which beetle in `card` is the rhinoceros beetle?

cards.title: Giraffe's cousin
cards.explain: The okapi has zebra-like stripes on its legs, but it is the only living relative of the giraffe. Zebras are horses, and tapirs are related to horses and rhinos.

jev.context: Three hoofed animals standing on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the closest living relative of the giraffe?

cards.title: Flamingo
cards.explain: The flamingo's thick bill bends sharply down in the middle. The roseate spoonbill is also pink but has a flat spoon-tipped bill, and the scarlet ibis has a thin curved bill.

jev.context: Three pink or red wading birds on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which bird in `card` is the flamingo?

cards.title: Hornbill
cards.explain: The hornbill wears a big casque, a helmet-like horn on top of its bill. The toucan has a huge bill with nothing on top, and the macaw is a parrot with a short hooked beak.

jev.context: Three big-billed birds perched on branches on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which bird in `card` is the hornbill?

cards.title: Sundew
cards.explain: The sundew catches insects on red hairs tipped with sticky droplets. The Venus flytrap snaps shut with toothed jaws, and the pitcher plant drowns insects in hanging cups.

jev.context: Three carnivorous plants on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which plant in `card` is the sundew?

cards.title: Peach
cards.explain: The peach is the fuzzy one with a seam down one side; peaches and apples are both in the rose family, like the pear.

jev.context: Three pieces of fruit on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which object in `card` is the peach?

cards.title: Lime
cards.explain: The lime has dimpled citrus peel and pointed ends like a lemon; the green apple is smooth with a stem, and limes actually turn yellow if left to ripen.

jev.context: Four pieces of fruit on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which object in `card` is the lime?

cards.title: Cheetah
cards.explain: Cheetahs have solid round spots and black tear lines down the face; leopards have small rosettes, and jaguars have big rosettes with dots inside.

jev.context: Three big spotted cats on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the cheetah?

cards.title: Whisk
cards.explain: The whisk is the balloon of looped wires; the one with a single wavy wire is a potato masher.

jev.context: Four steel kitchen utensils on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which object in `card` is the whisk?

cards.title: Croissant
cards.explain: The croissant is the crescent; the rectangular roll with chocolate peeking out is a pain au chocolat, made from the same laminated dough.

jev.context: Four baked goods on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which object in `card` is the croissant?

cards.title: Ukulele
cards.explain: Count the tuning pegs: the ukulele has four strings, the little guitar six, and the mandolin eight in pairs.

jev.context: Four string instruments on a white background in a two by two grid, all shown at the same size.
jev.instructions: Which object in `card` is the ukulele?

cards.title: Corgi
cards.explain: The corgi is the one with the very short legs and long body; the Shiba Inu and the Basenji both curl their tails over their backs.

jev.context: Three red and white dogs on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the corgi?

cards.title: Eiffel Tower
cards.explain: The Eiffel Tower stands on four legs joined by big arches; Prague's Petrin tower and England's Blackpool Tower were built in its image, and Tokyo Tower is painted orange and white for air safety.

jev.context: Four steel lattice towers on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which tower in `card` is the Eiffel Tower?

cards.title: Hedgehog
cards.explain: The hedgehog is the small one with short, tidy spines; the porcupine is a rodent with long quills and the echidna is an egg-laying mammal with a long snout.

jev.context: Three spiny animals on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the hedgehog?

cards.title: Macaron
cards.explain: The macaron (one o) is the French almond sandwich with ruffled feet. The coconut mound is a macaroon (two o's), the usual trap.

jev.context: Four cookies on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which object in `card` is the French macaron?

cards.title: Alpaca
cards.explain: The alpaca is the smaller, fluffier one with short spear-shaped ears; the llama is taller with long banana-shaped ears, and the camel has a hump.

jev.context: Three long-necked hoofed animals on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the alpaca?

cards.title: Sea lion
cards.explain: Sea lions have small ear flaps and prop themselves up on their front flippers; true seals like the spotted one have only ear holes and wriggle on their bellies, and the walrus has tusks.

jev.context: Three flippered marine mammals on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the sea lion?

cards.title: Tortoise
cards.explain: Tortoises live on land, with a high domed shell and stumpy elephant-like legs; the sea turtle has paddle flippers and the red-eared slider is a freshwater turtle with webbed feet.

jev.context: Three shelled reptiles on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the tortoise?

cards.title: Hoverfly
cards.explain: The hoverfly is a harmless fly dressed up as a wasp: huge eyes that cover most of its head, tiny stub antennae and only one pair of wings. Bees and wasps have long elbowed antennae and two pairs of wings.

jev.context: Three yellow and black striped insects on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which insect in `card` is the hoverfly?

cards.title: Moth
cards.explain: The moth has feathery antennae and a thick furry body; butterflies have thin antennae with little clubs at the tips.

jev.context: Three winged insects seen from above on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which insect in `card` is the moth?

cards.title: Samoyed
cards.explain: The Samoyed is the all-white, smiling one; the Siberian Husky and the heavier Alaskan Malamute are both grey and white.

jev.context: Three fluffy spitz-type sled dogs on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which dog in `card` is the Samoyed?

cards.title: Rigatoni
cards.explain: Rigatoni are wide ridged tubes cut straight across; penne are narrower tubes cut on a slant, like the nib of a pen.

jev.context: Four heaps of dry pasta on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which pasta in `card` is the rigatoni?

cards.title: Ciabatta
cards.explain: Ciabatta is the flat, floury, slipper-shaped Italian loaf with big holes inside; the baguette is long and thin, and the brioche is a rich, shiny loaf with a topknot.

jev.context: Three loaves of bread on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which bread in `card` is the ciabatta?

cards.title: Oboe
cards.explain: The oboe is played through a thin double reed sticking out of the top; the clarinet has a black beak-shaped mouthpiece with a single reed and a wider flared bell.

jev.context: Four woodwind instruments standing upright on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which instrument in `card` is the oboe?

cards.title: Ball-peen hammer
cards.explain: The ball-peen hammer has a rounded ball on the back of its head, for shaping metal; the claw hammer has a split claw for pulling nails.

jev.context: Four hammers with wooden handles on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which hammer in `card` is the ball-peen hammer?

cards.title: Big Ben
cards.explain: Big Ben's tower in London (the Elizabeth Tower) has its four clocks near the top under a dark pointed roof; the Kremlin's Spasskaya Tower is red brick with a star, and Mumbai's Rajabai Tower was modeled on Big Ben.

jev.context: Three clock towers on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which tower in `card` is Big Ben (the Elizabeth Tower in London)?

cards.title: Taj Mahal
cards.explain: The Taj Mahal is all white marble with four separate minarets at its corners; Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, which inspired it, is red sandstone, and Lahore's Badshahi Mosque is red with three domes.

jev.context: Three domed Mughal buildings on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which building in `card` is the Taj Mahal?

cards.title: Alligator
cards.explain: Alligators have a broad, rounded U-shaped snout; crocodiles have a narrower, pointed V-shaped one, and the gharial's snout is extremely thin.

jev.context: Three crocodilians seen from directly above on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the alligator?

cards.title: Gerbil
cards.explain: The gerbil has a long furry tail with a tuft at the end; hamsters have a tiny stub of a tail and guinea pigs have none.

jev.context: Three small pet rodents on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the gerbil?

cards.title: Emmental
cards.explain: Emmental is the Swiss cheese full of big round holes; Gouda has a smooth waxed rind and a dense inside, and Parmesan is a hard, grainy wheel with a dotted rind.

jev.context: Three cheeses on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which cheese in `card` is the Emmental?

cards.title: Nigiri
cards.explain: Nigiri is a hand-pressed mound of rice with a slice of fish laid on top; maki is rolled in seaweed and sliced, and sashimi is fish with no rice at all.

jev.context: Three servings of sushi and raw fish on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which one in `card` is the nigiri?

cards.title: Gyoza
cards.explain: Gyoza are thin-skinned Japanese dumplings pleated along one edge and pan-fried until the bottoms go crisp and brown; pierogi are thicker boiled half-moons with pressed edges, and bao are fluffy steamed buns.

jev.context: Three plates of dumplings on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which dumplings in `card` are the gyoza?

cards.title: Habanero
cards.explain: The habanero is the small orange chili shaped like a lantern; the jalapeno is a smooth green bullet, and bird's eye chilies are tiny, thin and red.

jev.context: Three kinds of chili pepper on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which pepper in `card` is the habanero?

cards.title: Mulberry
cards.explain: Mulberries are long and narrow and keep a thin green stem; blackberries are short and round, and raspberries are red and hollow where they came off the plant.

jev.context: Three small heaps of berries on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which berries in `card` are the mulberries?

cards.title: Pecan
cards.explain: The pecan is a long, smooth oval with neat reddish-brown ridges; walnut halves are paler, lumpy and shaped like a brain.

jev.context: Four kinds of shelled nuts on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which nut in `card` is the pecan?

cards.title: Acorn squash
cards.explain: The acorn squash is dark green with deep ribs and a pointed end, like a giant acorn; butternut is tan with a long neck, spaghetti squash is a smooth yellow oval, and the pumpkin is round and orange.

jev.context: Four winter squashes on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which squash in `card` is the acorn squash?

cards.title: Mandoline
cards.explain: A mandoline is a flat platform with a blade set across it, for slicing vegetables thin and even; the long rasp is a zester and the four-sided tower is a box grater.

jev.context: Four kitchen gadgets on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which tool in `card` is the mandoline (the kitchen slicer)?

cards.title: Australian plug
cards.explain: The Australian plug has two flat blades set at an angle like a V, plus an earth pin below; the UK plug has three thick rectangular pins, the US plug two parallel flat blades, and the Europlug two round pins.

jev.context: Four electrical plugs on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which plug in `card` is the Australian one?

cards.title: LED bulb
cards.explain: The LED bulb has a frosted dome on a thick ribbed neck that carries heat away from the chips; the incandescent bulb shows a glowing wire filament, and the compact fluorescent is a spiral tube.

jev.context: Three screw-in light bulbs on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which bulb in `card` is the LED bulb?

cards.title: Rugby ball
cards.explain: A rugby ball is fatter with blunt, rounded ends and has no laces; the American football is pointed with white laces, and the red Australian rules ball also has laces.

jev.context: Three oval balls on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which ball in `card` is the rugby ball?

cards.title: Canoe
cards.explain: A canoe is open on top and paddled with a single-bladed paddle; a kayak has a closed deck and a double-bladed paddle, and a rowing boat has a square stern and oars in oarlocks.

jev.context: Three small boats on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which boat in `card` is the canoe?

cards.title: BMX
cards.explain: The BMX is the small bike with 20-inch wheels and high straight handlebars; the road bike has curled drop handlebars and thin tyres, and the mountain bike has fat knobbly tyres and suspension.

jev.context: Three bicycles seen from the side on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which bicycle in `card` is the BMX?

cards.title: Bolt
cards.explain: A bolt has a hex head, an even machine thread and a blunt end, because it goes through a hole into a nut; a wood screw tapers to a sharp point, a nail has no thread, and a pop rivet has a pin sticking out of it.

jev.context: Four metal fasteners on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which fastener in `card` is the bolt?

cards.title: Locking pliers
cards.explain: Locking pliers (Vise-Grips) have a screw knob at the end of one handle and a release lever, so they clamp shut on their own; needle-nose pliers have long thin jaws and wire cutters have angled blades.

jev.context: Four kinds of pliers on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which tool in `card` is the locking pliers?

cards.title: Coupe glass
cards.explain: The coupe is the stemmed glass with a broad, shallow, rounded saucer of a bowl; the martini glass is a straight-sided V, the flute is tall and narrow, and the wine glass has a big round bowl.

jev.context: Four stemmed drinking glasses on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which glass in `card` is the coupe?

cards.title: States of matter
cards.explain: In a gas the particles are far apart and spread through the whole container. A solid is packed in a regular pattern, and a liquid is packed close but loosely at the bottom.

cards.title: Floating ice
cards.prompt: Which glass shows the ice cube right?
cards.explain: Ice (0.917 g/cm³) is a little less dense than water, so it floats with about 92% of it under the surface and only a thin slice above.

jev.context: Three glasses of water, each with one ice cube drawn at a different height.
jev.instructions: In `card`, which glass shows an ice cube sitting in water the way it really does?

cards.title: Bounce the beam
cards.prompt: The beam hits the mirror. Which target does it reach?
cards.explain: A mirror reflects light at the same angle it arrives. The beam meets the mirror at 60 degrees and leaves at 60 degrees on the other side, turning it 120 degrees, up and to the left, to target B.

jev.context: A laser on the left shines a red beam to the right onto a tilted flat mirror; three targets marked A, B and C are at the top.
jev.instructions: In `card`, after the beam reflects off the mirror, which target does it hit?

cards.title: Elephant's cousin
cards.explain: The rock hyrax looks like a big guinea pig, but hyraxes, together with manatees and dugongs, are the elephant's closest living relatives. The aardvark is a more distant African cousin, and the capybara is a rodent.

jev.context: Three mammals standing on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the closest living relative of the elephant?

cards.title: Not a fish
cards.prompt: Tap the one that is not a fish.
cards.explain: Despite its name, the cuttlefish is a mollusc, a cousin of squid and octopus. The seahorse is a bony fish, the whale shark is a shark and the manta is a ray, so all three are fish.

jev.context: Four sea animals on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is not a fish?

cards.title: Spider's cousin
cards.explain: The horseshoe crab is not a crab: like spiders and scorpions it is a chelicerate, with pincer-like mouthparts. Crabs are crustaceans and beetles are insects, and those two are closer to each other than to spiders.

jev.context: Three animals with hard shells seen from above on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the closest relative of a spider?

cards.title: Whale's cousin
cards.explain: Whales evolved from hoofed land mammals, and the hippo is their closest living relative. Seals are carnivores, related to dogs and bears, and the shark is a fish.

jev.context: Three animals on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is the closest living relative of the whales?

cards.title: Not a bear
cards.prompt: Tap the one that is not a bear.
cards.explain: The red panda is not a bear: it is the only living member of its own family. The giant panda and the sun bear are both true bears.

jev.context: Three furry mammals on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is not a bear?

cards.title: The bird
cards.explain: The penguin is a bird that cannot fly. The bat and the flying squirrel take to the air, but both are mammals with fur that feed their young on milk.

jev.context: Three animals on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which animal in `card` is a bird?

cards.title: The legume
cards.explain: The peanut grows in a pod under the ground, like a pea or a bean, so it is a legume. Walnuts, almonds and hazelnuts grow on trees.

jev.context: Four kinds of nuts on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which one in `card` is a legume?

cards.title: The fruit
cards.explain: To a botanist, a fruit grows from the flower and holds the seeds, so the tomato is a fruit. The carrot is a root and the potato is a tuber, a swollen underground stem.

jev.context: Three vegetables from the kitchen on a white background, side by side.
jev.instructions: Which one in `card` is botanically a fruit?

cards.title: The true berry
cards.explain: Botanically, a berry is a fleshy fruit grown from a single ovary with the seeds inside, and the banana is one. The strawberry's seeds sit outside on swollen flower tissue, and raspberries and blackberries are clusters of tiny fruits.

jev.context: Four fruits on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which fruit in `card` is a true berry in the botanical sense?

cards.title: Three flat pins
cards.explain: This is Type G, with three thick rectangular pins, the plug of the United Kingdom. Germany uses round-pin Types C and F, and the United States and Japan use flat-bladed Types A and B.

jev.context: One electrical plug on a white background.
jev.instructions: Which country uses the plug in `card`?

cards.title: Hexagon with three pins
cards.explain: This is Type J: a hexagonal plug with three round pins, the earth pin set below the other two. It is used in Switzerland; Germany and Austria use Types C and F, and Italy's own plug has its three pins in a straight line.

jev.context: One electrical plug on a white background.
jev.instructions: Which country uses the plug in `card`?

cards.title: Three pins in a row
cards.explain: This is Type L, with three round pins in a straight line, the earth in the middle. It is used in Italy; France uses Type E, Spain Types C and F, and Switzerland Type J, whose earth pin sits lower.

jev.context: One electrical plug on a white background.
jev.instructions: Which country uses the plug in `card`?

cards.title: Three round pins in a triangle
cards.explain: This is Type D, with three round pins in a triangle and a thicker earth pin on top. It is used in India; the United Kingdom uses Type G, Brazil Types C and N, and Japan Types A and B.

jev.context: One electrical plug on a white background.
jev.instructions: Which country uses the plug in `card`?

cards.title: Japanese plug
cards.prompt: Tap the plug used in Japan.
cards.explain: Japan uses Type A, two flat parallel blades, the same shape as in North America. The others are the United Kingdom's Type G, Switzerland's Type J and India's Type D.

jev.context: Four electrical plugs on a white background in a two by two grid.
jev.instructions: Which plug in `card` is the kind used in Japan?
